**RE: Member Appeal for Prior Authorization Denial**
*   **Patient Name:** Emerson Delgado
*   **Member ID:** W727121486
*   **Plan:** Regence BlueShield (Commercial/ACA), State of Washington
*   **Reference Number:** POC-A93FE7E3B5-95850
*   **Denied Service:** Lower back (lumbar) fusion (CPT 22612)
*   **Ordering Provider:** Reyes, MD, Orthopedic Surgery
*   **Date of Denial Notice:** 2026-08-07

Dear Appeals Committee,

I am writing to formally appeal the denial of prior authorization for a single-level lumbar spinal fusion (CPT 22612) to be performed by Dr. Reyes. The denial letter dated August 7, 2026, states that the "documentation submitted was incomplete and does not allow a determination of medical necessity." 

This letter and the attached clinical documentation resolve any perceived omissions. This appeal demonstrates that I fully satisfy the medical necessity criteria outlined in Regence BlueShield’s **Medical Policy Manual Surgery, Policy No. 187 ("Lumbar Spinal Fusion")**, effective July 1, 2026. 

Specifically, my condition meets all requirements under Section I.C of the policy for "**Spinal stenosis when all of the following Criteria are met**":

### 1. Neurogenic Claudication or Radicular Pain (Policy Criterion I.C.1)
*   **Policy Requirement:** *"Neurogenic claudication or radicular pain"*
*   **Clinical Evidence:** Clinical examinations by Dr. Reyes document a 14-month history of progressive, severe pain in my lower back and legs that is completely unrelieved by rest. Physical examinations reveal classic signs of neurogenic claudication, including diminished sensation in both L5 dermatomes.

### 2. Advanced Imaging Finding of Stenosis (Policy Criterion I.C.2)
*   **Policy Requirement:** *"Documented central, lateral recess, or foraminal stenosis, with or without disc protrusion/herniation, facet arthropathy or facet cyst, or ligamentum flavum hypertrophy on MRI or other advanced imaging consistent with the individual’s symptoms"*
*   **Clinical Evidence:** A lumbar spine MRI performed on May 29, 2026, formally documents severe central stenosis compressing the cauda equina, directly correlating to my bilateral leg pain, heaviness, and dermatomal sensory deficits.

### 3. Spondylolisthesis or High Likelihood of Instability (Policy Criterion I.C.3)
*   **Policy Requirement:** *"Spondylolisthesis at a level (L1-S1) to be included in the fusion demonstrated on x-rays, CT, or MRI..."*
*   **Clinical Evidence:** Flexion-extension radiographs and MRI dated May 29, 2026, demonstrate a grade I degenerative spondylolisthesis at the L4-L5 level with 5 mm of translational movement on flexion-extension views. This confirms segmental instability at the L4-L5 level targeted for fusion.

### 4. Significant Functional Impairment (Policy Criterion I.C.4)
*   **Policy Requirement:** *"There is either clinical documentation of significant functional impairment or disability, or objective measurement of severe disability using the Oswestry Disability Index tool"*
*   **Clinical Evidence:** Clinical records document severe functional impairment. Due to leg pain and a sensation of extreme heaviness, I am unable to stand or walk for more than 10 minutes before being forced to stop. This impairment is only relieved by sitting. [If your office utilizes the Oswestry Disability Index, the ODI score of __% is also attached to objectively support this severe disability].

### 5. Failure of at Least Three Months of Conservative Therapy (Policy Criterion I.C.5)
*   **Policy Requirement:** *"There is clinical documentation that a minimum of three months of conservative nonoperative therapy failed to adequately treat the individual’s current symptoms..."* including *"Physical therapy... and [t]wo or more of the following treatment modalities... Prescription anti-inflammatory medications... [or] Injection therapy..."*
*   **Clinical Evidence:** My symptoms have persisted for 14 months despite active conservative management, exceeding the three-month policy minimum:
    *   **Physical Therapy (Criterion I.C.5.b.i):** I completed a 10-week course of supervised physical therapy focusing on core stabilization and lumbar flexibility from May 7, 2026, through July 16, 2026, completing 16 total visits. This is fully documented in the attached physical therapy discharge note.
    *   **Prescription/Analgesic Medications (Criterion I.C.5.b.ii.a):** I trialed therapeutic-strength NSAIDs for 4 consecutive months, which failed to provide adequate pain relief.
    *   **Injection Therapy (Criterion I.C.5.b.ii.d):** I underwent a lumbar corticosteroid injection on May 18, 2026, which yielded only 4 weeks of partial, temporary relief before my baseline symptoms returned.

### 6. Nicotine-Free Status (Policy Criterion I.C.6)
*   **Policy Requirement:** *"The individual is nicotine-free OR there is clinical documentation that the individual has been abstinent from nicotine use for at least six weeks prior to planned procedure..."*
*   **Clinical Evidence:** Clinical records confirm that I am a lifelong non-smoker and am entirely nicotine-free.

### Conclusion and Documentation Enclosed
Because my clinical presentation, imaging, and extensive trial of conservative therapies align perfectly with the medical necessity definitions in Policy No. 187, the proposed lumbar fusion (CPT 22612) at L4-L5 is appropriate, necessary, and indicated. 

To resolve the "incomplete documentation" designation, the following records are attached to this appeal:
1.  Office visit notes from Dr. Reyes detailing 14 months of symptoms, physical exam findings, and functional limitations.
2.  Physical therapy discharge summary (16 visits, 2026-05-07 to 2026-07-16).
3.  Diagnostic reports for the lumbar MRI and flexion-extension X-rays dated 2026-05-29.
4.  Documentation of conservative medication trials (4 months of NSAIDs) and the corticosteroid injection note dated 2026-05-18.

Please review this completed clinical package and reverse this denial of prior authorization. If you require any additional information, please contact Dr. Reyes's office immediately at [Provider Phone Number].

Thank you for your prompt attention to this matter.

Sincerely,

Emerson Delgado
